replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: A second-order equation has an x squared term. First, move all terms to one side so the equation equals zero. Then, try factoring if possible. To find stationary points, take the derivative of f(x), which gives you dy/dx. Set that equal to zero and solve for x. These are your critical points. Then plug each x value back into the original function to get the corresponding y values. These (x,y) pairs are your stationary points.
